title: Design System: Francis Yambao, game developer

cobalt-line.status: declared in :root, not yet painted by any shipped rule

ink-dim.status: declared in :root, not yet painted by any shipped rule

display.purpose: Selected game name on the stage; also Continue? and the VS splash name. Uppercase, skewed -8deg.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the dossier title. Uppercase, skewed -8deg from bottom-left.

intro.purpose: Select-screen h1. Uppercase, balanced wrap, upright.

title.purpose: Move names and career roles (career steps up to clamp(1.8rem, 3vw, 2.5rem)).

label.purpose: Short yellow block headings (Choose a game, Loadout, Build notes) and fact values. Sentence case.

button.purpose: Button faces and HUD nav; 1.45rem on big buttons.

stat.purpose: Stat-slot labels, P1 cursor, tile names.

lead.purpose: Opening paragraphs of the player profile and Continue?.

small.purpose: Chips, tags, fact labels, stat values, footer (0.85–0.95rem).

slant.purpose: skewX applied to every plate: buttons, arrows, chips, tags, tile names, cursor, section titles, wipes.

unslant.purpose: Counter-skew on the inner face so text and icons stand upright inside a slanted plate.

cut.purpose: Section-edge triangle height, 100vw × tan(8deg). Clip-path polygon(0 100%, 100% 0, 100% 100%), background: inherit, bottom: calc(100% - 1px).

parallelogramFormula.value: offset = tan(8deg) × height / width = 0.1405 × h / w; polygon(o 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - o) 100%, 0 100%)

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: Dossier dialog over its rgba(14, 12, 43, 0.88) backdrop.

shadows.name: ghost-stroke
shadows.purpose: Ghost button outline inside the skewed plate.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Default focus everywhere; ink outline inside the red Continue? section.

shadows.name: focus-clipped
shadows.purpose: Focus on clip-path tiles; traces the parallelogram where an outline would be clipped.

motion.name: stage-wipe
motion.value: 440ms ease-swap; red slab skewX(-8deg) translateX(-130%) → 0 (hold 40–55%) → 130%; repaint at 170ms

motion.name: roster-preview-delay
motion.purpose: Hover (fine pointer) or focus on a tile previews it on the stage.

motion.name: vs-splash
motion.value: 900ms ease-swap; slab holds 36–62%; name slides from +40vw, holds 38–58%, exits to -40vw; dossier revealed at 380ms
motion.purpose: Opening a game into its dossier.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation/transition-duration 0.01ms; scroll-behavior auto; no stage wipe; no VS splash; no autoplay

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: HUD nav hides; select screen stacks; roster 3 columns; move list and dossier single column.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: HUD 60px; stage and stage card display: contents, reordered intro → screen → name → roster → tagline → stats → open; roster becomes scroll-snap strip at 42% tiles.

sectionSequence.edge: cobalt-deep slab behind stage, polygon(0 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 14vh) 100%, 0 100%)

components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 1.15rem; border: 0; background: var(--red-deep, #d42a1f); color: var(--cream, #fff6e0); font-family: var(--display, "Big Shoulders Display", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.01em; text-decoration: none; transform: skewX(-8deg); transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-face { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; transform: skewX(8deg); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-icon { width: 1.15em; height: 1.15em; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2.2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-btn-red:hover { background: #c42319; transform: skewX(-8deg) translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-red:active { transform: skewX(-8deg) translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-red:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--yellow, #ffc93c); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Roster Tile (current)
components.description: Selectable fighter tile: 16:10 parallelogram frame; current state floods red with a P1 cursor; focus traced by yellow drop-shadows.
components.css: .ds-tile { display: block; width: 240px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: none; filter: drop-shadow(3px 0 0 #ffc93c) drop-shadow(-3px 0 0 #ffc93c) drop-shadow(0 3px 0 #ffc93c) drop-shadow(0 -3px 0 #ffc93c); } .ds-tile-frame { position: relative; display: block; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; padding: 5px; background: var(--ink, #0e0c2b); clip-path: polygon(8.8% 0, 100% 0, 91.2% 100%, 0 100%); transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tile-art { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #3c3e62, #1c1950); clip-path: polygon(8.8% 0, 100% 0, 91.2% 100%, 0 100%); filter: saturate(0.85) brightness(0.88); } .ds-tile-name { position: absolute; z-index: 1; left: 10%; bottom: 12%; padding: 0.1rem 0.55rem; background: var(--ink, #0e0c2b); color: var(--cream, #fff6e0); font-family: var(--display, "Big Shoulders Display", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 900; line-height: 1.2; text-transform: uppercase; transform: skewX(-8deg); } .ds-tile-cursor { position: absolute; z-index: 1; top: 9%; right: 12%; padding: 0.05rem 0.5rem; background: var(--yellow, #ffc93c); color: var(--ink, #0e0c2b); font-family: var(--display, "Big Shoulders Display", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 1.05rem; font-weight: 900; line-height: 1.2; opacity: 0; transform: skewX(-8deg) scale(0.6); transition: opacity 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tile.is-current .ds-tile-frame { background: var(--red, #f23a2e); } .ds-tile.is-current .ds-tile-art { filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.15) brightness(1.05); background: linear-gradient(135deg, #e93025, #810102); } .ds-tile.is-current .ds-tile-name { font-size: 1.5rem; } .ds-tile.is-current .ds-tile-cursor { opacity: 1; transform: skewX(-8deg) scale(1); }

narrative.overview:
The whole site is a fighting-game roster screen that still scrolls and clicks like a normal page. Every shipped game is a fighter: a slanted tile on the roster, its footage on a slanted stage, its name in huge condensed caps. A flat, saturated cobalt field owns most of the page; deep ink is the stage and the HUD; P1 red marks what is selected and what to press; ready yellow marks focus, cursors, and the small labels that orient a skimmer. Cream carries the words.

One angle runs the system. Every vertical edge leans 8° forward (`skewX(-8deg)`), and every section boundary climbs 8° to the right (`100vw × tan 8°`). Panels, tiles, stats, chips, buttons, wipes, and the VS splash all share that lean, so the page reads as one cabinet rather than a collection of styled boxes. The density is arcade, not editorial: big blocks of flat color, short heavy type, tight gutters between tiles, and motion that happens as a single decisive sweep rather than a scatter of small effects.

Depth comes from color stacking (ink on cobalt, cobalt-deep behind the stage, red flooding the current tile), not from soft card shadows. Nothing is rounded.
keyCharacteristics: One angle everywhere: -8deg lean on verticals, +8° climb on section edges.
Flat saturated grounds: cobalt, cobalt-deep, ink, red, in a fixed section sequence.
Selection is flooded, not outlined: the current tile turns red and gets a yellow P1 cursor.
Condensed heavy caps for names and headings; Rubik for anything read as a sentence.
Slanted plates, upright text: the shape leans, the words stay straight.
Motion is one diagonal red slab, used for stage swaps and the VS splash, and removed entirely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Flooded Selection Rule
rules.body: The current thing is shown by flooding its surface red, never by a thin ring alone. A selected tile, a selected thumb, a primary button: red fills it.

rules.name: The Red Carries Ink Rule
rules.body: Text set directly on P1 red is ink, or cream only at display size (the Continue? title). Any red surface that holds button-size cream text uses red-deep instead.

rules.name: The Yellow Points Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks where you are and what to read next (focus, cursor, labels, section titles on deep grounds). It never fills a large surface.

rules.name: The Caps Are Names Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for names and titles set in the display face (games, sections, moves, roles). Labels, buttons, and every Rubik line stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Lean Is For Names Rule
rules.body: Display type that names something (the stage name, section titles, the dossier title, Continue?, tile names) is skewed -8deg from its bottom-left corner. Reading text never leans.

rules.name: The Flat Plates Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows, tiles, chips, and stats carry no shadow. Separation comes from a different ground color and the gap between slanted plates.

dos: **Do** lean every new panel, tile, chip, and button at the one angle: `skewX(-8deg)` for plates, `tan 8° × height / width` for clipped parallelograms of known ratio.
**Do** keep text upright inside a skewed plate by counter-skewing the face (`skewX(8deg)`).
**Do** show the current item by flooding it red (`red`) and marking it with the yellow P1 cursor, not by an outline alone.
**Do** use `red-deep` for any red surface that carries button-size cream text.
**Do** draw focus on clipped elements with yellow `drop-shadow` filters so the ring follows the parallelogram; use the 3px yellow outline everywhere else.
**Do** join a new section to the one above with the `cut` triangle in its own ground, and add `cut` to the previous section's bottom padding.
**Do** keep reading text in Rubik at 34–60ch and names and headings in Big Shoulders Display.
**Do** make any new motion a single diagonal red sweep on the swap curve, and give it an instant path under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** round any corner; the system has no radius.
**Don't** introduce a second deliberate angle; slants, wipes, and section edges are all designed to 8°.
**Don't** set cream body-size text directly on P1 red.
**Don't** put soft shadows on panels, rows, tiles, or chips; separation is by ground color and gap.
**Don't** skew reading text or set Rubik in uppercase.
**Don't** fill large areas with yellow; it marks focus and labels only.
